explanation: Tchaikovsky discovered the newly invented celesta in Paris in 1891 and asked his publisher to keep it secret, so that other Russian composers would not use it first.

claims.text: The melody of the Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy in Tchaikovsky's The Nutcracker is played on the celesta.
The melody of the Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy is not played on a glockenspiel, a harp or a xylophone.
Tchaikovsky came across the celesta in Paris in 1891.
The celesta had been invented shortly before, by Auguste Mustel, who patented it in 1886.
Tchaikovsky asked his publisher to keep the celesta secret so that other Russian composers, such as Rimsky-Korsakov and Glazunov, would not use it before him.
